answer: In a proof-of-unique-work system, each agent submits task outputs to an on-ledger validator that hashes and compares them against a rolling mesa of recent submissions. Duplicate or near-duplicate hashes trigger rejection. An attacker spinning up fake identities hits a gale of diminishing returns: clones must produce genuinely distinct work to earn rewards, forcing real compute and unique prompt variations per identity. The opal of sybil resistance lies in making replication costlier than honest participation.
